guarantee.sentence: Shiryaev-Roberts mixture e-detector on the bounded-bet increment 1 + lambda*clip(r, +-3)/3 over +-{0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.9} (ADR 0031; Shin-Ramdas-Rinaldo 2022 Thm 2.4): E_inf[N*] >= 1/alpha_arl at alpha_arl = 1e-3 for every pre-change law whose AR(1)-whitened, standardized residual is conditionally mean-zero AFTER clipping at +-3 -- symmetric laws at any tail and any scale error, at oracle or estimated (m >= 30) parameters, phi <= 0.9, any changepoint. The heavy-tailed nulls N5 (lognormal), N6 (t3) and N8 (AR(1) with t3 innovations) are CLAIMED inside the regime; the standardized lognormal's clipped mean (about -0.028) is the one known departure from the premise and the S2 cell decides it. Delay after a K1 canonical step is at most D*(alpha_arl, delta_eff) evaluated at the bounded increment's growth rate (Amendment v1.C77: 34.9 ticks at phi = 0), registered as a floor and not claimed as a theorem about the increment mixture.

quantifiers.text: every pre-change law with a conditionally mean-zero clipped residual in the claimed regime, any changepoint
delay under the bounded D* at every phi <= 0.9

regime.nulls: iid-gaussian, ar1-gaussian (phi <= 0.9), estimated moments and phi, lognormal, t3, ar1-t3 (combined stress)

shipped_path.kind: e-detector (SR mixture of bounded-bet increments over 8 lambdas), AR(1) pre-whitened, alarm at M_t >= 1/alpha_arl; exported through ./detectors/* behind ESrMeanShiftParams.increment = 'bounded' (default 'gaussian' unchanged), NO shipped compile path (no engine surface dispatches either e-SR, so S1 is MISSING by construction and the USE, if issued, is USE under the scorer's non-blocking reading of S1)
shipped_path.notes: ADR 0031: ValidityEnvelope.statistic 'e-detector'; assertValidForFdrPath refuses it under every assertion. The increment needs no sub-Gaussian premise: E[g | F] = 1 whenever the clipped residual is conditionally mean-zero. The price is delay: growth rate 0.344 at 1.5 sigma against the Gaussian increment's 1.125 (study 2026-09-e-sr-bounded H2).

falsifier: an in-regime S2 cell (N1-N8, heavy tails included) with arl0_T + 1.645*arl0_se < 1/alpha_arl, or an in-regime K1-canonical delay cell with delay_canonical + 1.645*delay_se > D*(alpha_arl, delta_eff, 'bounded')
